messages.content: You are an AML analyst assistant. Answer only from the provided documents. Cite the exact typology and rule. If the documents do not support an answer, say so. Output is advisory; a human must approve any filing.

<DOCUMENT id="aml/layering.md">Layering separates illicit proceeds from their source through chains of transfers. The rule fires on three or more pass-through hops where inbound and outbound amounts match within 2% and the balance is held for less than 48 hours.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT id="aml/trade-based-laundering.md">Trade-based laundering hides value inside mis-invoiced trade documents.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT id="card/card-not-present.md">Card-not-present fraud is unauthorised remote use of stolen card credentials.</DOCUMENT>

Question: Funds moved through three accounts in under 48 hours with inbound and outbound amounts matching within 1%. Which typology and is it SAR-ready?

##Reason: Three pass-through hops, near-identical in/out amounts (within 1%), balance held under 48 hours — this matches the layering rule in aml/layering.md exactly (≥3 hops, in/out within 2%, held <48h). It is layering, not trade-based (no trade instrument) and not card fraud. The pattern is grounded and the typology and rule are named, so the case is SAR-ready pending human authorisation. ##Answer: Typology: layering. The layering/pass-through rule is breached (3 hops, in/out within 2%, held <48h). The alert is SAR-ready; escalate to the nominated officer for human approval before filing.
